changes.text: At Haran, Jehovah, understood by Latter-day Saints as the premortal Jesus Christ, promises Abraham that his family will carry the gospel and priesthood to all nations. These blessings reach every family: salvation and eternal life. Those who receive the gospel are counted among Abraham’s seed.

Later, Jesus tells Nathanael that he will see heaven open and angels ascending and descending upon the Son of Man. Read beside Jacob’s dream, this shared imagery invites us to ponder how Jesus Christ brings us near to God.

Other prophetic visions widen this hope. Enoch hears of Zion’s people meeting in a joyful embrace and dwelling with the Lord. John sees a new heaven and earth, with God among His people and death and sorrow ended. Their distinct visions invite hope in God’s lasting presence.

Read Revelation 21:1–4 directly: new heaven/earth, New Jerusalem, God with His people, end of death/sorrow/pain. Distinct prophetic visions remain separate from words spoken to Abraham.
